papers.summary: Analyzes how GD, Adam-like, Muon, Shampoo, and K-FAC update geometry changes singular-mode birth, decay, and effective-rank trajectories in matrix factorization. Its broader regression experiment finds different transient spectra despite similar final fits.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses how optimization shapes weight spectra and low-rank bias, while remaining a model-based rather than LLM-scale result.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws for Euclidean GD, coordinate-wise updates of SignGD and an instantaneous Adam approximation, spectral updates of Muon and cumulative Shampoo, and a block curvature model of K-FAC.
All methods reach comparable final loss and final spectra of W W despite substantially different transient dynamics shown by the stable rank and effective rank throughout training.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Learns low-rank projection subspaces jointly against model-output KL while keeping pretrained weights frozen. At 70% compression on Llama-2-7B, it reports WikiText-2 perplexity of 10.9 versus 13.3 for the strongest baseline.
papers.relevance: Tests preservation of LLM quality under low-rank weight factorization. It is post-training compression, not evidence that pretraining itself improves compressibility.

evidence.quote: All projectors are optimized jointly against a global objective—the KL divergence to the dense model’s output distribution or the model’s original training loss—while the pretrained weights remain frozen.
At − 70 % -70\% compression, LSP brings Llama-2-7B to 10.9 10.9 WikiText-2 perplexity and 42.2 % 42.2\% mean zero-shot accuracy, versus 13.3 13.3 and 36.0 % 36.0\% for the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression

papers.summary: Uses module-matched, paired-seed LoRA rank sweeps under label noise. In its Qwen2.5-7B classification experiment, every sampled rank, including parameter parity, has higher test NLL than dense fine-tuning of the same modules.
papers.relevance: Combines LoRA rank, practical language-model fine-tuning, and generalization under noisy labels.

evidence.quote: We quantify this relation under label noise on four vision backbones and a 7 7 B language model with a module-matched rank sweep (MMRS), which extends past full rank and compares every rank with dense fine-tuning of the same modules, paired by seed.
Every sampled rank, parity included, remains behind dense in all three seeds, while the valley reference reads Rec > 1 \mathrm{Rec}>1 at every sampled rank from r = 448 r{=}448 on.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: Proposes a fixed-rank-manifold LoRA optimizer that accounts for factorization gauge symmetry. Reported supervised fine-tuning results show lower validation loss, while some downstream accuracy differences are small relative to seed variation.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimization geometry and practical language-model behavior of low-rank updates.

evidence.quote: Our optimizer applies row and column normalization in a conditioning frame defined by the left singular vectors of the tangent momentum, projects the resulting direction back onto the tangent space, and retracts to the fixed-rank manifold.
RoM obtains the highest mean accuracy on both downstream benchmarks for the Llama models, although the differences are small relative to variation across seeds.

papers.title: Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr{ö}m Sketching

papers.summary: Compares two spectral-preconditioning variants with AdamW, Muon, and MANO across GPT-2, LLaMA, and Qwen3 pretraining. At LLaMA-1.3B scale, NormPre-L reports validation loss of 2.8662 versus Muon’s 2.9037, with peak memory approximately equal to Muon’s and a shorter end-to-end step time.
papers.relevance: Connects Newton–Schulz and sketched spectral optimization to measured quality, throughput, and GPU-memory tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: Within each setting, all optimizers use matched model initialization, data order, training budget and evaluation protocol.

papers.title: Normalize-Then-Precondition: A Hierarchical Approach to Marginal Scale and Interaction Geometry for LLM Training

papers.summary: Introduces author-judged retrieval of prior papers relevant to research questions. It reports 0.42 Recall@20 for agentic search versus 0.48 for embedding retrieval and identifies candidate coverage as a limiting factor.
papers.relevance: Directly informs retrieval and relevance-ranking decisions for the user’s research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: We introduce a retrieval task with author-provided judgments: given an initial research question, retrieve these papers from only the literature available when the project began.
Agentic search does no better than embedding retrieval (0.42 vs. 0.48 Recall@20) despite calling that same retriever as a tool.
Stronger rerankers benefit more from better candidate coverage.

papers.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research

limitations: The cited performance results come from the papers’ reported experiments, not independent replication.
The spectral-dynamics paper studies matrix factorization and regression, not measured LLM weight compressibility.
LSP compresses pretrained weights after training rather than testing training-induced compressibility.
The larger NormPre model results are single runs under matched budgets.
Clean’s 1.3B learning-rate comparison used a shortened sweep; its reported 13B feasibility should not be conflated with the measured 1.3B comparison.
Code availability and reproducibility were not verified. X analysis was disabled.
